title: Why Did a Change When We Edited b?
learning_goal: Explain name binding, shared references, mutation and copying lists.
code:
a = [1, 2]
b = a
b.append(3)
print(a)

a = [1, 2]
b = a.copy()
b.append(3)
print(a)
quiz: After b = a, does b.append(3) change a?
answer: Yes: both names refer to the same list object.
transfer: Replace b = a with b = a.copy(), then mutate b. Explain the difference.
caveat: An assignment binds a name to an object; it does not copy the object. list.copy() creates a shallow copy.

title: Python == vs is: Same Value, Same Object?
learning_goal: Distinguish equality from object identity without unsafe integer-interning demonstrations.
code:
a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2]
print(a == b)
print(a is b)
quiz: Why does a == b return True but a is b return False?
answer: Their contents compare equal, but they're distinct list objects.
transfer: Assign c = a and compare both c == a and c is a.
caveat: Don't use small integer/string interning as an identity lesson; use separately created mutable lists.

title: Python Negative Indexes Explained Visually
learning_goal: Read negative indexing from the end of a sequence.
transfer: Try colors[-3]. Predict the value before running.
caveat: Negative indexing does not wrap indefinitely; out-of-range indices raise IndexError.

title: Why range(5) Stops at Four
learning_goal: Understand start-inclusive, stop-exclusive ranges and step size.
answer: No. The stop value is excluded.
caveat: range is a range object; list(range(...)) materializes its values for display.

title: Python Slicing: The Right Edge Is Excluded
learning_goal: Understand start-inclusive, stop-exclusive slicing and reversal.
quiz: Which letters are returned by letters[1:4]?
answer: b, c, d; index four is excluded.
caveat: Slicing returns a new list for a list input; it does not mutate the original list.

title: Python List vs Tuple: What Can Change?
learning_goal: Distinguish mutable lists from immutable tuples.
code:
numbers = [1, 2]
numbers.append(3)
print(numbers)
fixed = (1, 2)
try:
    fixed.append(3)
except AttributeError:
    print("tuple has no append")
quiz: Can you call append on a tuple?
answer: No, a tuple does not support append.
transfer: Try putting a list inside a tuple; observe that the contained list can still mutate.
caveat: Tuple immutability does not make nested mutable objects immutable.

title: Python Truthiness Is Not the Same as Equality
learning_goal: Distinguish truth testing of 0, None, empty collections and nonempty strings.
expected:
int False
NoneType False
str False
list False
str True
answer: True: it is a nonempty string.
caveat: Falsy values are not interchangeable; 0, None, empty lists and empty strings differ in type and meaning.

title: Python dict.get vs Square Brackets
learning_goal: Distinguish missing-key KeyError from .get default behavior.
transfer: Set profile['role']='builder' and run both lookups again.
caveat: .get() returns the default for missing keys, but may also return None when a present key maps to None.

title: Python enumerate: Position Plus Value
learning_goal: Pair sequence values with indexes, including a configurable start.
quiz: What number is paired with A when start=1?
caveat: enumerate tracks an index counter; it doesn't modify the input sequence.

title: List Comprehension: Filter and Transform
learning_goal: Compare a filtered list comprehension with the equivalent loop.
code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4]
via_loop = []
for n in numbers:
    if n % 2 == 0:
        via_loop.append(n * n)
via_comp = [n * n for n in numbers if n % 2 == 0]
print(via_loop)
print(via_comp)
quiz: Which original values survive the even-number filter?
transfer: Change the predicate to n % 2 != 0 and predict the result.
caveat: Comprehensions do not replace every loop. Use an ordinary loop when readability or multiple effects matter.
